children: is seeing success with the relaunch of its Mr. Pibb brand. After returning with a new recipe late last year, Mr. Pibb broke out to become the fastest-growing brand in 2026. Overall purchase consideration jumped more than 11 percentage points, according to a Morning Consult poll.

The revived Mr. Pibb features 30% more caffeine and a bold, spicy cherry taste with hints of caramel. A Mr. Pibb Zero Sugar version was also part of the brand refresh. The relaunch included new packaging, as well as marketing efforts that included online videos, social content, and grassroots events. Those efforts seemed to have paid off as popularity has surged across baby boomers, Generation X, and millennials. Mr. Pibb also gained traction with Generation Z, although to a lesser degree.
Mr. Pibb began in 1972 as Coca-Cola's
pepper-style soft-drink competitor to Dr Pepper

first used the name Peppo in a limited Memphis launch, but legal pressure from Dr Pepper led the company to revise the product and introduce Mr. Pibb in test markets, including Dr Pepper's hometown of Waco, Texas. Mr. Pibb developed a following as a cherry-spice alternative to cola and root beer, often positioned as a more irreverent, challenger-style soda. In 2001, Coca-Cola

reformulated and renamed the drink Pibb Xtra, emphasizing a bolder “spicy cherry” profile. While distribution later fell sharply as retail momentum faded, the limited availability was enough to preserve a cult following.
